bug_semantics: Tor conflux shares one conflux_t (cfx) across all legs of a set. linked_circuit_closed() removes a closing linked leg and, when it is the last remaining leg, deletes the cfx from the linked pool but deliberately leaves circ->conflux pointing at that still-alive object so linked_circuit_free() can free it later. A recovery leg for the same nonce (conflux_launch_leg -> unlinked_get_or_create) reuses that same cfx with is_for_linked_set. When the recovery leg later finishes linking (conflux_process_linked -> try_finalize_set -> cfx_add_leg), it re-adds the cfx to the linked pool and sets recovery->circ->conflux to it, creating two distinct circuits that both own the same object: the already-closed last original leg (not yet reaped) and the revived recovery leg. On post-loop reap, linked_circuit_free() on the first empty-legs circuit calls conflux_free(cfx); the second circuit then dereferences circ->conflux->legs (heap UAF) and would otherwise conflux_free again (double free). A malicious exit can drive link -> recover -> close last linked leg -> relink recovery -> close/reap to crash the client. CWE-911 / TROVE-2026-026 / bug 41306.
flaw_origin: The dual-owner close-then-revive lifetime was written in the original Prop#329 conflux pool, 336a24754d117b46793ce6824e35ff6b7962bf9d (David Goulet, committed by Mike Perry, 2023-04-06). That first-write added src/core/or/conflux_pool.c as a new file containing (1) last-leg keep of circ->conflux in linked_circuit_closed, (2) recovery-leg cfx sharing via unlinked_get_or_create/linked_pool_get + is_for_linked_set, and (3) try_finalize_set revival via linked_pool_add + leg->circ->conflux = unlinked->cfx. linked_circuit_free already transferred ownership to a still-unlinked recovery set, but linked_circuit_closed never did, so a recovery that links in the close-to-free window becomes a second owner. Public history has no finer parent of those lines: parent 2f865b4bba1bedc96f17b696916d74c392c83e1b has no conflux_pool.c. Vendor annotation is bugfix on 0.4.8.1-alpha, the first release containing this commit.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-77587 / TROVE-2026-026 is a published (not withdrawn) client crash via conflux cfx UAF/double-free when a recovery leg revives a set after its last linked leg has closed but not yet been freed. The first-party 0.4.9.11 ChangeLog and changes/bug41306 pin the mechanism, the attack (malicious exit), and the introduced-in version 0.4.8.1-alpha. The patched lines in 7477e8bf28dfc858ac6e93afceabc654893533d8 close exactly that gap in linked_circuit_closed by handing cfx ownership to a still-unlinked recovery set, mirroring the existing free-path transfer. BIC search used -S/-L/blame on those last-leg-keep, unlinked_get_or_create sharing, and try_finalize_set revival lines, not an AI-commit hunt. All of them first appear in 336a24754d117b46793ce6824e35ff6b7962bf9d, the Prop#329 pool add that created src/core/or/conflux_pool.c; the immediate parent tree lacks that file, so the vulnerable lines are absent before the BIC. That commit is the smallest surviving public first-write (one parent, not a merge/backport/release squash, no reconstructable finer members). It is an ancestor of the affected 0.4.8.1-alpha tag; the fix is in 0.4.9.11 and not in 0.4.9.10.
